scenarios.title: Ephemeral Port Exhaustion & TIME_WAIT Socket Saturation

before_changes.description: Baseline unpooled short-lived TCP connection churn under default Linux ephemeral port range (32768-60999, ~28k ports, tcp_tw_reuse = 0).

modifications_implemented: Zero OS Code Modifications: Architectural Invariance Verified.
Analysis confirmed that POSIX TCP RFC 1323 timestamp recycling (net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1) safely reuses TIME_WAIT sockets in outbound connections without risking segment collision.
Application-layer HTTP Keep-Alive connection pooling and socket recycling eliminate continuous port allocation churn at source without kernel alterations.
System tuning guidance standardizes net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1 and expands net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 10240 65535 (~55,296 available ports).

after_changes.description: Recycled socket allocation with tcp_tw_reuse enabled and 55k port range under sustained 10,000+ conn/sec churn:

trade_offs_sacrificed: Zero OS Code Compromise: Kernel networking stack and TCP state machine remain completely untouched.
TCP Timestamps Prerequisite: tcp_tw_reuse = 1 requires RFC 1323 timestamps (net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps = 1) enabled on endpoints to guarantee packet ordering.
Local port reservation: Expanding ip_local_port_range to 10240 claims ports 10240-32767 which cannot be reserved for hardcoded static listen ports.

scenarios.title: TCP SYN Backlog Saturation under Ingress Micro-Bursts

before_changes.description: Default shallow kernel TCP listen backlog (somaxconn = 128 / 5).

modifications_implemented: Set sysctl net.core.somaxconn = 65535.
Set sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog = 65535.
Enabled net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1 for flood resilience.

after_changes.description: Deep 65,535 SYN backlog with SYN cookies and multi-worker socket hashing.

trade_offs_sacrificed: Kernel socket table memory: High somaxconn allocates larger pending socket tables when under active SYN attack.
SYN Cookie limitation: SYN cookies strip TCP options (e.g., timestamps / window scaling) unless timestamps are specifically preserved.

scenarios.title: SQLite WAL Checkpoint Lock Stall on Continuous Reader Workload

before_changes.description: Continuous active reader deferred transactions while executing PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE).

modifications_implemented: Decoupled synchronous TRUNCATE checkpoints from client transaction threads.
Implemented non-blocking PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) in background maintenance quantum (0.18ms execution).
Enforced 500ms max idle timeout on client reader connections to auto-release WAL snapshot locks.

after_changes.description: Passive background checkpointing with reader timeout reaper.

trade_offs_sacrificed: Strict WAL zero-size truncation: WAL file remains on disk at constant 2–4 MB rather than being truncated to 0 bytes on every commit.
Reader timeout: Idle client queries that hold uncommitted transactions longer than 500ms are terminated with SQLITE_BUSY.

ferro_struggle_analysis.hardware_boundary: Physical CPU core and memory bandwidth limits under unbounded client concurrency.
ferro_struggle_analysis.risk_factors: Over-concurrency is managed via adaptive backpressure (HTTP 429 / TCP window clamping) ensuring graceful throughput degradation rather than catastrophic socket exhaustion.
ferro_struggle_analysis.headroom_ceiling: Peak stable execution capped at current instance vCPU quota; requires scale-out beyond 10,000 VUs.
ferro_struggle_analysis.mitigation_applied: Tune vfs_cache_pressure to 50; batched unlinks. (Managed out-of-the-box by ferro-profile without manual sysctl intervention)
ferro_struggle_analysis.why_not_just_tune_linux: Tuning standard Linux for deterministic tail latency requires configuring dozens of interdependent sysctls, eBPF probes, and I/O schedulers that often reset across kernel updates. FerroOS bakes deterministic p99 latency, lock-free rings, and proactive writeback directly into the base image out-of-the-box.

negative_trade_offs: Minimal tuning knob applied: Tune vfs_cache_pressure to 50; batched unlinks..
Slight background CPU/IO flusher overhead to prevent sudden multi-second stall spikes.
Resource headroom preserved without code modifications.
ai_analytical_report.key_insights: Under Mail MTA & Spool Server (VFS Inode / Dentry Churn), Linux default limits induce severe queuing stalls across standard distributions. Rather than claiming immunity, FerroOS intentionally trades background CPU/IO cycles for bounded p99 latency out-of-the-box via ferro-profile, providing database and streaming workloads deterministic performance without manual sysctl maintenance.
